sub_scenario.family: rapid live troubleshooting leadership versus careful asynchronous incident analysis
sub_scenario.one_line: dam safety instrumentation specialist: reject an input-uncertain standing role

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the sensor correlation sheet and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The reservoir log review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can explain a confirmed gauge trend to the maintenance crew.
Are routine technical briefings difficult?
No, once the readings are cross-checked.
Someone new shadowed me in the inspection trailer this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the spillway alarms into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
After a seepage anomaly, I compared piezometer history, rainfall records, and inspection photos, then scheduled the correct drain inspection before pressure rose.
What made the plan fit?
The instruments were connected to the physical observation.
I can draft an inspection priority after reviewing the day’s sensor files.
Why is that reliable?
I can compare rainfall, flow, and gauge drift without a live alarm.
I archived last cycle's notes on the reservoir log and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The emergency operations call expects a spillway action recommendation before the downstream warning message is issued.
Can you wait for a full inspection?
No, the warning timing is fixed.
A vendor call about the sensor correlation sheet ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the inspection trailer checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the spillway alarms.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the reservoir log records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
During a live spillway alarm, I treated a rising piezometer as structural movement and urged an unnecessary gate change; a clogged sensor line was found later.
What was the faulty connection?
I equated one instrument's movement with the dam's movement.
I sketched next week's plan for the spillway alarms before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the sensor correlation sheet updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The field technician can clear the sensor line and provide a photo comparison before the operations call, but only if access conditions permit.
Would that settle your role?
It would if the clearance and comparison are actually complete.
The emergency manager says the public needs an authoritative voice on the call.
Does authority verify the instrument?
No, it cannot replace the check.
I closed the week by updating the inspection trailer handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Emergency management asks whether I should be designated as the live spillway adviser. What should I tell them?
